papers.title: Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits
papers.abstract: Abstract Mechanistic understanding of how networks of neurons carry out neural computations requires knowledge of their underlying synaptic connectivity. However, current methods for reconstructing synaptic connections are extremely laborious and typically limited to mapping connections between nearby neurons. Here we developed Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics (BRISC), which uses rabies viruses carrying random molecular barcodes to map both local and long-range monosynaptic inputs of hundreds of neurons in parallel. To ensure that the majority of post-synaptic starter neurons are uniquely labeled with distinct barcode sequences, we generated libraries of rabies viruses with sufficient diversity to label >1000 neurons and controlled the probability of barcode transmission between starter neurons by limiting their density. We applied BRISC to map inputs of single neurons in the mouse primary visual cortex. We read out the expression of viral barcodes in rabies-infected neurons in situ, preserving spatial information. We then matched barcode sequences between starter and presynaptic neurons, mapping the inputs of 385 neurons and identifying 7,814 putative synaptic connections, revealing layer- and cell-type-specific local connectivity rules and topographic organization of long-range inputs. These results show that BRISC can simultaneously resolve the synaptic connectivity of hundreds of neurons, enabling reconstruction of neural circuits at an unprecedented scale.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for a more efficient method to map synaptic connectivity in neural circuits, as current techniques are laborious and limited to local connections. The background highlights the importance of understanding how neural networks perform computations through their synaptic architecture.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a novel method called Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics (BRISC) to map both local and long-range monosynaptic inputs of neurons in the mouse primary visual cortex. The method was applied to single neurons in this specific brain region.
analysis.methods: BRISC utilizes rabies viruses with random molecular barcodes to label neurons, allowing for the simultaneous mapping of synaptic connections. The technique involves reading viral barcode expression in infected neurons and matching sequences between starter and presynaptic neurons to determine connectivity.
analysis.main_results: The method successfully mapped the inputs of 385 neurons and identified 7,814 putative synaptic connections, revealing layer- and cell-type-specific local connectivity rules and the topographic organization of long-range inputs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these results as demonstrating the capability of BRISC to resolve synaptic connectivity at an unprecedented scale, offering a significant advancement in neural circuit reconstruction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for neuroscience research, enabling more comprehensive studies of neural circuits and their functional organization, which could inform future investigations into neural computation and disease mechanisms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mouse primary visual cortex and does not address broader applications or other neural regions. The evidence is strong as it directly reports the successful application of BRISC in mapping synaptic connections with high precision.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces BRISC, a novel method using rabies viruses with random molecular barcodes to map synaptic connectivity in neural circuits. The technique enables the simultaneous resolution of local and long-range monosynaptic inputs, providing insights into layer- and cell-type-specific connectivity rules in the mouse primary visual cortex. The results demonstrate the potential of BRISC to reconstruct neural circuits at an unprecedented scale, advancing our understanding of neural computation. However, the study is limited to a specific brain region and does not explore broader applications. The evidence is strong, as it directly reports the successful implementation of BRISC in identifying synaptic connections with high precision.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决对更有效的方法来映射神经回路中突触连接的需求,因为当前的技术非常费力并且仅限于局部连接。背景强调了理解神经网络如何通过其突触架构执行计算的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一种名为条形码 狂犬病 原位连接组学 (BRISC) 的新方法,用于绘制小鼠初级视觉皮层神经元的局部和远程单突触输入图。该方法适用于该特定大脑区域的单个神经元。
elements_zh.methods: BRISC 利用带有随机分子条形码的 狂犬病病毒 来标记神经元,从而可以同时映射突触连接。该技术涉及读取受感染神经元中的病毒条形码表达以及匹配起始神经元和突触前神经元之间的序列以确定连接性。
elements_zh.main_results: 该方法成功映射了 385 个神经元的输入,并识别了 7,814 个假定的突触连接,揭示了特定于层和细胞类型的局部连接规则以及远程输入的拓扑组织。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对神经科学研究具有重要意义,可以对神经回路及其功能组织进行更全面的研究,这可以为未来对神经计算和疾病机制的研究提供信息。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for a more efficient method to map synaptic connectivity in neural circuits, as current techniques are laborious and limited to local connections. The background highlights the importance of understanding how neural networks perform computations through their synaptic architecture.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study developed a novel method called Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics (BRISC) to map both local and long-range monosynaptic inputs of neurons in the mouse primary visual cortex. The method was applied to single neurons in this specific brain region.
analysis_en.methods: BRISC utilizes rabies viruses with random molecular barcodes to label neurons, allowing for the simultaneous mapping of synaptic connections. The technique involves reading viral barcode expression in infected neurons and matching sequences between starter and presynaptic neurons to determine connectivity.
analysis_en.main_results: The method successfully mapped the inputs of 385 neurons and identified 7,814 putative synaptic connections, revealing layer- and cell-type-specific local connectivity rules and the topographic organization of long-range inputs.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these results as demonstrating the capability of BRISC to resolve synaptic connectivity at an unprecedented scale, offering a significant advancement in neural circuit reconstruction.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for neuroscience research, enabling more comprehensive studies of neural circuits and their functional organization, which could inform future investigations into neural computation and disease mechanisms.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mouse primary visual cortex and does not address broader applications or other neural regions. papers.title_zh: 用于神经回路高通量重建的条码 狂犬病 原位连接组学
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Mechanistic understanding of how networks of neurons carry out neural computations requires knowledge of their underlying synaptic connectivity. However, current methods for reconstructing synaptic connections are extremely laborious and typically limited to mapping connections between nearby neurons. Here we developed Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics (BRISC), which uses rabies viruses carrying random molecular barcodes to map both local and long-range monosynaptic inputs of hundreds of neurons in parallel. To ensure that the majority of post-synaptic starter neurons are uniquely labeled with distinct barcode sequences, we generated libraries of rabies viruses with sufficient diversity to label >1000 neurons and controlled the probability of barcode transmission between starter neurons by limiting their density. We applied BRISC to map inputs of single neurons in the mouse primary visual cortex. We read out the expression of viral barcodes in rabies-infected neurons in situ, preserving spatial information. We then matched barcode sequences between starter and presynaptic neurons, mapping the inputs of 385 neurons and identifying 7,814 putative synaptic connections, revealing layer- and cell-type-specific local connectivity rules and topographic organization of long-range inputs. These results show that BRISC can simultaneously resolve the synaptic connectivity of hundreds of neurons, enabling reconstruction of neural circuits at an unprecedented scale.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 要从机制上理解神经元网络如何进行神经计算,需要了解其潜在的突触连接性。然而,当前重建突触连接的方法非常费力,并且通常仅限于映射附近神经元之间的连接。在这里,我们开发了条形码 狂犬病 原位连接组学 (BRISC),它使用携带随机分子条形码的 狂犬病病毒 并行映射数百个神经元的局部和远程单突触输入。为了确保大多数突触后起始神经元都用不同的条形码序列进行唯一标记,我们生成了具有足够多样性的 狂犬病病毒 文库来标记 > 1000 个神经元,并通过限制起始神经元的密度来控制起始神经元之间条形码 传播 的概率。我们应用 BRISC 来绘制小鼠初级视觉皮层中单个神经元的输入图。我们原位读出了 狂犬病 感染的神经元中病毒条形码的表达,保留了空间信息。然后,我们匹配起始神经元和突触前神经元之间的条形码序列,映射 385 个神经元的输入并识别 7,814 个假定的突触连接,揭示特定于层和细胞类型的局部连接规则以及远程输入的拓扑组织。这些结果表明,BRISC 可以同时解析数百个神经元的突触连接,从而能够以前所未有的规模重建神经回路。

papers.full_text: Abstract Rabies remains a formidable global public health challenge, attributable to viruses of the genus Lyssavirus. Control efforts have progressed markedly through the introduction of inactivated vaccines, rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), which collectively provide both pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP and PEP). In low-resource environments, however, PEP implementation is hindered by the lack of highly sensitive diagnostic assays. At present, the gold-standard techniques endorsed by the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and the World Health Organization (WHO) — namely the Rapid Fluorescent Focus Inhibition Test (RFFIT) and the Fluorescent Antibody Virus Neutralization (FAVN) assay — are employed to quantify rabies virus neutralizing antibody (VNA) titers. These assays, nonetheless, are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and necessitate handling of live virus. This review elucidates emerging methodologies for antibody quantification against rabies virus. Notably, the recent advancement of an Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) — characterized by rapid turnaround, high specificity and sensitivity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability has significantly enhanced detection of antibodies directed against the rabies virus glycoprotein. We also discuss the principle technical obstacles encountered during the assay development. Looking forward, these innovations are poised to improve both the accuracy and throughput of rabies serology, thereby streamlining efficacy evaluations and prophylaxis monitoring, and ultimately bolstering global rabies control and eradication initiatives. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Rabies remains a formidable global public health challenge, attributable to viruses of the genus Lyssavirus. Control efforts have progressed markedly through the introduction of inactivated vaccines, rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), which collectively provide both pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP and PEP). In low-resource environments, however, PEP implementation is hindered by the lack of highly sensitive diagnostic assays. At present, the gold-standard techniques endorsed by the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) and the World Health Organization (WHO) — namely the Rapid Fluorescent Focus Inhibition Test (RFFIT) and the Fluorescent Antibody Virus Neutralization (FAVN) assay — are employed to quantify rabies virus neutralizing antibody (VNA) titers. These assays, nonetheless, are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and necessitate handling of live virus. This review elucidates emerging methodologies for antibody quantification against rabies virus. Notably, the recent advancement of an Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) — characterized by rapid turnaround, high specificity and sensitivity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability has significantly enhanced detection of antibodies directed against the rabies virus glycoprotein. We also discuss the principle technical obstacles encountered during the assay development. Looking forward, these innovations are poised to improve both the accuracy and throughput of rabies serology, thereby streamlining efficacy evaluations and prophylaxis monitoring, and ultimately bolstering global rabies control and eradication initiatives. papers.title_original: Rabies: a brief note on diagnostics and prophylactics

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study addresses the need for improved diagnostic methods for rabies virus, particularly in low-resource settings where current techniques are limited by their complexity and requirements for live virus handling.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of methodologies for rabies virus diagnostics and prophylactics, focusing on human and animal rabies, with an emphasis on vaccine quality control and antibody detection in vaccinated individuals.
analysis.methods: The study discusses the development and validation of ELISA techniques for quantifying rabies virus glycoprotein antibodies, as well as real-time RT-PCR assays for rabies virus quantification in vaccines and the use of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for rabies virus diagnosis in cerebrospinal fluid.
analysis.main_results: The study reports the development of a novel ELISA for measuring glycoprotein in human rabies vaccines and the validation of a real-time RT-PCR assay for rabies virus quantification. It also highlights the use of metagenomic sequencing for rabies virus detection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as significant advancements in rabies diagnostics, offering more efficient and scalable methods for antibody detection and virus quantification, which could improve vaccine quality control and serological monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These innovations can enhance the accuracy and speed of rabies diagnostics, particularly in resource-limited areas, and support better vaccine monitoring and public health initiatives for rabies control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a review of existing methodologies and does not present original experimental data, which limits the strength of the evidence. However, it provides a comprehensive overview of current and emerging diagnostic techniques.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the challenges and advancements in rabies diagnostics and prophylactics, emphasizing the need for improved methods in low-resource settings. It highlights the limitations of traditional assays like RFFIT and FAVN, which are labor-intensive and require live virus handling. The study discusses the development of ELISA techniques for antibody quantification, real-time RT-PCR for virus detection, and metagenomic sequencing for etiological diagnosis. These innovations are interpreted as significant steps toward more accurate and scalable diagnostic tools, which could enhance vaccine quality control and public health initiatives. The findings suggest that these methods may improve rabies serology and monitoring, supporting global rabies control efforts. However, the study is based on a review rather than original data, which limits the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究解决了对 狂犬病病毒 改进诊断方法的需求,特别是在资源匮乏的环境中,当前技术因其复杂性和活病毒处理的要求而受到限制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了 狂犬病病毒 诊断和预防方法,重点关注人类和动物 狂犬病,重点是 疫苗 质量控制和接种个体的抗体检测。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究讨论了用于定量 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白抗体的 ELISA 技术的开发和验证,以及用于 疫苗 中 狂犬病病毒 定量的实时 RT-PCR 测定,以及脑脊液中 狂犬病病毒 诊断 宏基因组下一代测序的使用。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告了一种用于测量人类 狂犬病 疫苗 糖蛋白的新型 ELISA 的开发,以及对 狂犬病病毒 定量的实时 RT-PCR 测定的验证。它还强调了使用宏基因组测序进行 狂犬病病毒 检测。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为 狂犬病 诊断的重大进步,为抗体检测和病毒定量提供了更有效和可扩展的方法,这可以改善 疫苗 的质量控制和血清学监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些创新可以提高 狂犬病 诊断的准确性和速度,特别是在资源有限的地区,并支持更好的 疫苗 监测和 狂犬病 控制的公共卫生举措。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于对现有方法的回顾,没有提供原始实验数据,这限制了证据的强度。然而,它提供了当前和新兴诊断技术的全面概述。

papers.title: Epidemiological profile of dog bite cases and rabies in Guinea, 2018-2019
papers.abstract: Introduction: In Guinea, between 2011 and 2017, there were 95 clinical canine rabies cases, 10,153 cases of bites recorded in the health facilities, and 50 clinical human rabies cases recorded in the veterinary post. The profile of the disease is not well known. This study describes the epidemiological profile of rabies to guide the decision-making of the Ministries of Health and Livestock. Methods: A descriptive incidence study was carried out using January 2018–August 2019 bite and rabies databases of the Ministries of Health and Livestock. We calculated median age, frequency, and district bite incidence per 100,000 population. Results: Overall, 1,953 bite cases were recorded, with an incidence of 10 per 100,000 population and a median age of 14 years. Of those bitten, 75% (1458/1953) benefited from post-exposure vaccination (PEV); none of the 10 rabid humans sought vaccination, and all died. Of the 1,662 biting dogs followed up, 937 (56%) were observed, of which 159 (17%) developed rabies symptoms and were euthanised, and 27 (17%) were sampled, 20 (74%) of which were confirmed for rabies by PCR test. N’Zérékoré and Fria had an incidence of >50 bites per 100,000 inhabitants; 40% of canine rabies cases were from Faranah. Fifteen thousand dogs were vaccinated in districts with high incidence and percentage of confirmed rabies cases. Conclusion: People under 15 years old were most affected. We suggest improving dog bite and rabies surveillance in the district with low incidence, building laboratory sampling capacity, testing suspected canine cases, and conducting an exhaustive census among the dog population.
papers.journal: Journal of Interventional Epidemiology and Public Health

The study provides important insights for public health decision-making but lacks detailed statistical or laboratory analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在几内亚,2011年至2017年期间,卫生机构记录了95例临床犬狂犬病病例,10,153例咬伤病例,兽医站记录了50例临床人类狂犬病病例。该疾病的概况尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用卫生部和畜牧业部 2018 年 1 月至 2019 年 8 月的咬合和 狂犬病 数据库进行了一项描述性 发病率 研究。总体而言,记录了 1,953 起咬伤病例,发病率 为每 100,000 人中有 10 起,中位年龄为 14 岁。

papers.title_zh: 几内亚2018-2019年犬咬伤病例及狂犬病的流行病学特征
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: In Guinea, between 2011 and 2017, there were 95 clinical canine rabies cases, 10,153 cases of bites recorded in the health facilities, and 50 clinical human rabies cases recorded in the veterinary post. The profile of the disease is not well known. This study describes the epidemiological profile of rabies to guide the decision-making of the Ministries of Health and Livestock. Methods: A descriptive incidence study was carried out using January 2018–August 2019 bite and rabies databases of the Ministries of Health and Livestock. We calculated median age, frequency, and district bite incidence per 100,000 population. Results: Overall, 1,953 bite cases were recorded, with an incidence of 10 per 100,000 population and a median age of 14 years. Of those bitten, 75% (1458/1953) benefited from post-exposure vaccination (PEV); none of the 10 rabid humans sought vaccination, and all died. Of the 1,662 biting dogs followed up, 937 (56%) were observed, of which 159 (17%) developed rabies symptoms and were euthanised, and 27 (17%) were sampled, 20 (74%) of which were confirmed for rabies by PCR test. N’Zérékoré and Fria had an incidence of >50 bites per 100,000 inhabitants; 40% of canine rabies cases were from Faranah. Fifteen thousand dogs were vaccinated in districts with high incidence and percentage of confirmed rabies cases. Conclusion: People under 15 years old were most affected. We suggest improving dog bite and rabies surveillance in the district with low incidence, building laboratory sampling capacity, testing suspected canine cases, and conducting an exhaustive census among the dog population.

papers.title: PERCEPÇÃO SOBRE RAIVA E INTERAÇÃO ENTRE OS HABITANTES DO MUNICÍPIO DE CHÃ GRANDE - PE PERCEPTION OF RABIES AMONG THE INHABITANTS OF CHÃ GRANDE MUNICIPALITY - PE PERCEPCIÓN SOBRE LA RABIA ENTRE LOS HABITANTES DEL MUNICIPIO DE CHÃ GRANDE - PE
papers.abstract: A raiva é uma zoonose viral de elevada letalidade, cuja persistência no ciclo silvestre representa um desafio para a saúde pública, especialmente em áreas rurais com intensa interação entre humanos, animais domésticos e fauna silvestre. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a percepção da população rural de Chã Grande, Pernambuco, sobre a raiva, caracterizar as interações com mamíferos silvestres e seus potenciais riscos epidemiológicos. A pesquisa foi realizada por entrevistas com moradores da zona rural, investigando o conhecimento sobre a doença, práticas relacionadas ao contato com animais domésticos e silvestres e as espécies envolvidas nessas interações. Os dados foram analisados considerando a relevância epidemiológica das espécies citadas. Os resultados indicaram que a maioria dos entrevistados reconhece a raiva como doença grave e fatal. Foram relatadas interações frequentes com mamíferos silvestres, incluindo caça e avistamentos recorrentes, com destaque para o tatu e a raposa, esta última integrante do ciclo silvestre terrestre da raiva. Também foram mencionadas espécies sem relevância epidemiológica direta, evidenciando lacunas na percepção do risco sanitário associado à fauna silvestre. Conclui-se que essas interações configuram risco potencial para a manutenção do ciclo da raiva, reforçando a necessidade de ações educativas, vigilância integrada e estratégias no âmbito da Saúde Única.
authors: Georgia Cybelle dos Santos Silva Barros
papers.journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to analyze the perception of rabies among rural residents of Chã Grande, Pernambuco, focusing on interactions with wild mammals and their epidemiological risks. The research was conducted through interviews with rural inhabitants, exploring their knowledge about the disease, practices involving contact with domestic and wild animals, and the species involved in these interactions. The findings indicated that most participants recognized rabies as a severe and fatal disease. Frequent interactions with wild mammals, such as hunting and recurring sightings, were reported, with the fox being highlighted as part of the terrestrial wild cycle of rabies. The study also noted the mention of species without direct epidemiological relevance, highlighting gaps in the perception of health risks associated with wild fauna. The authors concluded that these interactions pose a potential risk for maintaining the rabies cycle, emphasizing the need for educational actions, integrated surveillance, and strategies within the framework of Unified Health. The evidence is based on interviews and qualitative analysis, and the study provides insights into public perception and potential risk factors for rabies transmission in rural areas.

papers.source_body_en: A raiva é uma zoonose viral de elevada letalidade, cuja persistência no ciclo silvestre representa um desafio para a saúde pública, especialmente em áreas rurais com intensa interação entre humanos, animais domésticos e fauna silvestre. A pesquisa foi realizada por entrevistas com moradores da zona rural, investigando o conhecimento sobre a doença, práticas relacionadas ao contato com animais domésticos e silvestres e as espécies envolvidas nessas interações. Os dados foram analisados considerando a relevância epidemiológica das espécies citadas. Os resultados indicaram que a maioria dos entrevistados reconhece a raiva como doença grave e fatal. Conclui-se que essas interações configuram risco potencial para a manutenção do ciclo da raiva, reforçando a necessidade de ações educativas, vigilância integrada e estratégias no âmbito da Saúde Única.
papers.abstract_zh: 狂犬病是一种高致死率的人兽共患病,其在野生动物循环中的持续存在对公共卫生构成挑战,尤其是在人类、家畜和野生动物互动频繁的农村地区。本研究旨在分析巴西佩恩塔布斯州查格兰德地区农村居民对狂犬病的认知,描述其与野生动物的互动情况及其潜在的流行病学风险。研究通过与农村居民的访谈进行,调查他们对狂犬病的了解、与家畜和野生动物接触的相关行为以及涉及的物种。数据根据所提及物种的流行病学重要性进行分析。结果显示,大多数受访者认识到狂犬病是一种严重且致命的疾病。报告了频繁与野生动物的互动,包括狩猎和反复的目击,其中刺猬和狐狸尤为突出,后者是狂犬病陆地野生动物循环的一部分。还提到了一些无直接流行病学意义的物种,显示出农村居民对野生动物相关卫生风险的认知存在不足。结论认为,这些互动可能构成维持狂犬病循环的潜在风险,强调了开展健康教育、综合监测和单一卫生体系策略的必要性。

papers.title: From one-size-fits-all to context-specific: the 10-day observation rule-a need for change
papers.abstract: WHO’s ‘Zero by 30’ strategic plan relies on post-exposure prophylaxis guidelines designed for high-resource settings. This policy brief argues that the implementation gap of the 10-day observation rule in high-burden countries stems from fundamental infeasibility, exposing two paradigm defects in WHO guideline development: one-size-fits-all thinking and insufficient attention to implementation science. When the public misinterprets the 10-day rule as “wait and see” rather than “initiate PEP immediately while observing the animal,” three biological facts render this misinterpretation fatal: symptomatic rabies is nearly 100% fatal and untreatable; a single vaccine dose cannot promptly induce sufficient neutralizing antibodies; and the incubation period for craniofacial Category III bites can be as short as 5–10 days—shorter than the full observation window. Waiting for animal observation without initiating PEP during this window means missing the only opportunity for effective prevention. Evidence from multiple countries shows that the rule’s preconditions are almost never met in settings where 95% of rabies deaths occur. This misinterpretation has led to preventable deaths and given rise to guideline-associated rabies phobia (GARP). We propose five revisions to refine—not discard—the rule. Reshaping the paradigm is an ethical prerequisite for achieving ‘Zero by 30’.

The authors highlight the misinterpretation of the 10-day observation rule as a ‘wait and see’ approach rather than a prompt intervention strategy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a policy brief analyzing the implementation gap of the 10-day observation rule in high-burden countries, where 95% of rabies deaths occur. It focuses on the misinterpretation of the rule and its consequences for rabies prevention.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of evidence from multiple countries showing the rule’s preconditions are rarely met. The authors also examine the biological facts that make the misinterpretation of the rule dangerous, such as the near 100% fatality rate of symptomatic rabies and the limitations of a single vaccine dose.
analysis.main_results: Evidence from multiple countries shows that the rule’s preconditions are almost never met in settings where 95% of rabies deaths occur. Waiting for animal observation without initiating PEP during this window means missing the only opportunity for effective prevention.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the misinterpretation of the 10-day rule has led to preventable deaths and rabies phobia. They propose five revisions to the rule to address these issues, emphasizing the need for context-specific guidelines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for context-specific rabies prevention strategies, particularly in high-burden countries, to ensure effective post-exposure prophylaxis and reduce preventable deaths.

papers.title: Guideline Adherence of Post-Exposure Prophylaxis and Factors Associated with Vaccine Series Completion in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Rabies-Risk Exposure
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate adherence to national guidelines in rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administered to patients presenting with rabies-risk exposures to the emergency department, and to identify factors associated with completion of the vaccine series.Methods: Records of 343 patients presenting to the Emergency Department of Ağrı Training and Research Hospital between June 2025 and May 2026 were reviewed. The distribution of continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test; the Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Adherence of the administered prophylaxis to the 2019 Turkish Ministry of Health Rabies Prophylaxis Guideline was evaluated.Results: The median age of patients was 21.0 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 10.0-34.0), and 62.1% were male. Overall guideline adherence of the administered prophylaxis was found to be 54.5%; among Category III/IV exposures with an indication for rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), RIG was administered in only 14.0% of cases. The vaccine series completion rate was 72.9%, and among the 14 variables examined, only a history of prior prophylaxis was found to be significantly associated with completion (p=0.014). Rural residence, atypical exposure types, and milder wound categories were associated with longer delays in presentation to the emergency department, and presentations increased markedly during summer months.Conclusion: Adherence of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis practices to national guidelines, particularly regarding the indication for rabies immunoglobulin, was found to remain below the desired level. Strengthening physician education and reviewing RIG accessibility in the region were considered necessary

source_records.title: Guideline Adherence of Post-Exposure Prophylaxis and Factors Associated with Vaccine Series Completion in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Rabies-Risk Exposure
source_records.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate adherence to national guidelines in rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administered to patients presenting with rabies-risk exposures to the emergency department, and to identify factors associated with completion of the vaccine series.Methods: Records of 343 patients presenting to the Emergency Department of Ağrı Training and Research Hospital between June 2025 and May 2026 were reviewed. The distribution of continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test; the Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Adherence of the administered prophylaxis to the 2019 Turkish Ministry of Health Rabies Prophylaxis Guideline was evaluated.Results: The median age of patients was 21.0 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 10.0-34.0), and 62.1% were male. Overall guideline adherence of the administered prophylaxis was found to be 54.5%; among Category III/IV exposures with an indication for rabies immunoglobulin (RIG), RIG was administered in only 14.0% of cases. The vaccine series completion rate was 72.9%, and among the 14 variables examined, only a history of prior prophylaxis was found to be significantly associated with completion (p=0.014). Rural residence, atypical exposure types, and milder wound categories were associated with longer delays in presentation to the emergency department, and presentations increased markedly during summer months.Conclusion: Adherence of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis practices to national guidelines, particularly regarding the indication for rabies immunoglobulin, was found to remain below the desired level. Strengthening physician education and reviewing RIG accessibility in the region were considered necessary

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated adherence to national rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) guidelines and factors associated with vaccine series completion in patients presenting to the emergency department with rabies-risk exposures. A total of 343 patients were reviewed between June 2025 and May 2026. Overall guideline adherence was 54.5%, with only 14.0% of Category III/IV exposures receiving rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) when indicated. Vaccine series completion was 72.9%, with prior prophylaxis history being the only significant factor associated with completion. Delays in presentation were linked to rural residence, atypical exposure types, and milder wounds, with increased presentations during summer months. The study concluded that adherence to guidelines remains suboptimal and emphasized the need for physician education and improved RIG accessibility.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究旨在回顾性评估对急诊科就诊的 狂犬病 风险暴露患者进行 狂犬病 暴露后预防 (PEP) 的国家指南的遵守情况,并确定与完成 疫苗 系列相关的因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 使用 Shapiro-Wilk 检验评估连续变量的分布;Mann-Whitney U、Kruskal-Wallis、卡方和 Fisher 精确检验用于组间比较。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 评估了所实施预防措施对 2019 年土耳其卫生部 狂犬病 预防指南的遵守情况。所采取预防措施的总体指南依从率为 54.5%;在需要使用 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白 (RIG) 的 III/IV 类暴露中,仅 14.0% 的病例使用了 RIG。发现 狂犬病 暴露后预防 实践对国家指南的遵守情况,特别是关于 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白的适应症,仍低于所需水平。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 疫苗系列的完成率为72.9%,在检查的14个变量中,仅发现既往预防史与完成率显着相关(p=0.014)。农村居住、非典型暴露类型和较轻的伤口类别与到急诊室就诊的较长时间延迟有关,并且在夏季,就诊时间明显增加。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强医生教育并审查该地区RIG的可及性被认为是必要的。

papers.title: Investigating Primary Motor Cortex Involvement in Mouse Vocal Communication
papers.abstract: Vocal communication is used to transmit a range of information to other individuals. While many vocalizations are innate, some species can learn to change their vocal output. This is termed vocal-learning, and it is a rare trait and a necessary building block for human spoken language and songbird song. Comparative work in humans and songbirds suggests that convergent genetic and neural specializations may drive these learned vocal behaviors. Two key features of these advanced vocal learners are: i) specialized primary motor regions in the forebrain with activity tied to vocalization; and ii) dense monosynaptic projections from the primary motor cortex to brainstem vocal motor neurons. Work from our lab suggests that the mouse ultrasonic vocalization (USV) system has some features similar to those found in advanced vocal learners. USV production is innate, but mice show context-dependent changes in their syllable repertoire. Mice may also possess a rudimentary laryngeal motor cortex (LMC), with a sparse direct projection to laryngeal motor neurons in the nucleus ambiguus (Amb) and sparse populations with short-latency functional control over vocal musculature. Prior to these studies, mice have been assumed to lack any cortical involvement in the production of ultrasonic vocalizations. The limited behavioral flexibility of mouse song and evidence of forebrain representations of vocal muscles suggest that vocal learning may exist over a continuum, with mice being at the limited end of the continuum, able to exert some cortical control over USV production. This hypothesis argues that vocal learning is not an all-or-nothing ability, but exists on a continuous range of vocal behavior, supported by a corresponding range of neural and genetic specializations. In this thesis, I proposed to test the continuum hypothesis, by investigating whether there is a role of primary motor cortex in mouse vocal behavior. I first characterized the role of the sparse direct projection in the control of vocal muscles. I used replication-deficient rabies tracing to confirm that there is a sparse projection from layer 5 neurons of LMC to brainstem laryngeal motor neurons, and also found that an anterior M1 region, orofacial motor cortex (OMC), also has a direct cortico-motoneuronal projection. I then used PLXNA1fl/fl;RBP4-CRE transgenic mice, which have denser innervation from the cortex to Amb, to test the functional consequences of enhancement of this circuit. I used paired intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) and electromyography (EMG) and found faster responses in the larynx of these mice to cortical stimulations. These findings show that the enhancement of direct cortico-motoneuronal projections produce faster cortical control over vocal muscles. I then tested whether mouse M1 has any neural activity associated with vocalization behavior. I combined electrophysiological recordings in LMC and OMC with video and audio monitoring of freely behaving and vocalizing males. I identified sparse populations of neurons with activity modulated over the production of bouts of USVs. This is the first report of vocalization-related activity in mouse M1. Finally, I developed a novel method to identify individual USV sources in pairs of vocalizing mice. This method used wearable miniature microphones to detect and assign USVs to a single animal based on simple amplitude differences. I reliably identified the individual responsible for the vocalization, and found that female mice produce far fewer USVs in a male- female pair than previously assumed. This method allows further study of the inter-individual vocal dynamics and behavior during the production of social USV. Overall, my findings support the continuum hypothesis of vocal learning. The direct cortical input from M1 to laryngeal motor neurons appears to be an evolutionary node to have faster control of vocal musculature. These same M1 regions have limited but present populations with vocalization-associated activity. This suggests that a sparse cortical representation for vocal muscles may be conserved. These results provide greater insight into the cortical control of vocalization in the mammalian brain and the evolution of more advanced vocal learning.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether the primary motor cortex plays a role in mouse vocal behavior, building on the hypothesis that vocal learning exists on a continuum with mice at the limited end.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using transgenic mice with enhanced cortical innervation to the brainstem vocal motor neurons, as well as freely behaving male mice for vocalization monitoring.
analysis.methods: The methods included replication-deficient rabies tracing to map cortical projections, paired intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) and electromyography (EMG) to assess functional consequences, and wearable miniature microphones to identify individual ultrasonic vocalization (USV) sources.
analysis.main_results: The study found that there is a sparse direct projection from the layer 5 neurons of the laryngeal motor cortex (LMC) to brainstem laryngeal motor neurons, and an anterior M1 region, orofacial motor cortex (OMC), also has a direct cortico-motoneuronal projection. Additionally, sparse populations of neurons in M1 showed activity modulated during USV production.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the direct cortical input from M1 to laryngeal motor neurons may represent an evolutionary node for faster control of vocal musculature, and that M1 regions have limited but present populations with vocalization-associated activity, supporting the continuum hypothesis of vocal learning.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide greater insight into the cortical control of vocalization in the mammalian brain and the evolution of more advanced vocal learning, which may inform future studies on vocal behavior and its neural basis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single species and the use of a transgenic model, but the findings are supported by direct experimental evidence and provide a novel method for identifying individual USV sources.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the primary motor cortex in mouse vocal behavior, testing the hypothesis that vocal learning exists on a continuum. Using transgenic mice with enhanced cortical projections and behavioral monitoring, the research identifies sparse direct projections from the laryngeal motor cortex (LMC) to brainstem motor neurons and vocalization-related activity in M1 regions. These findings suggest that mice may have a rudimentary form of cortical control over vocalization, supporting the continuum hypothesis. The study also introduces a novel method for identifying individual ultrasonic vocalization (USV) sources. While the results are supported by direct experimental evidence, the study is limited by its focus on a single species and the use of a transgenic model.

papers.title_zh: 研究小鼠声音交流中初级运动皮层的参与
papers.source_body_en: Vocal communication is used to transmit a range of information to other individuals. While many vocalizations are innate, some species can learn to change their vocal output. This is termed vocal-learning, and it is a rare trait and a necessary building block for human spoken language and songbird song. Comparative work in humans and songbirds suggests that convergent genetic and neural specializations may drive these learned vocal behaviors. Two key features of these advanced vocal learners are: i) specialized primary motor regions in the forebrain with activity tied to vocalization; and ii) dense monosynaptic projections from the primary motor cortex to brainstem vocal motor neurons. Work from our lab suggests that the mouse ultrasonic vocalization (USV) system has some features similar to those found in advanced vocal learners. USV production is innate, but mice show context-dependent changes in their syllable repertoire. Mice may also possess a rudimentary laryngeal motor cortex (LMC), with a sparse direct projection to laryngeal motor neurons in the nucleus ambiguus (Amb) and sparse populations with short-latency functional control over vocal musculature. Prior to these studies, mice have been assumed to lack any cortical involvement in the production of ultrasonic vocalizations. The limited behavioral flexibility of mouse song and evidence of forebrain representations of vocal muscles suggest that vocal learning may exist over a continuum, with mice being at the limited end of the continuum, able to exert some cortical control over USV production. This hypothesis argues that vocal learning is not an all-or-nothing ability, but exists on a continuous range of vocal behavior, supported by a corresponding range of neural and genetic specializations. In this thesis, I proposed to test the continuum hypothesis, by investigating whether there is a role of primary motor cortex in mouse vocal behavior. I first characterized the role of the sparse direct projection in the control of vocal muscles. I used replication-deficient rabies tracing to confirm that there is a sparse projection from layer 5 neurons of LMC to brainstem laryngeal motor neurons, and also found that an anterior M1 region, orofacial motor cortex (OMC), also has a direct cortico-motoneuronal projection. I then used PLXNA1fl/fl;RBP4-CRE transgenic mice, which have denser innervation from the cortex to Amb, to test the functional consequences of enhancement of this circuit. I used paired intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) and electromyography (EMG) and found faster responses in the larynx of these mice to cortical stimulations. These findings show that the enhancement of direct cortico-motoneuronal projections produce faster cortical control over vocal muscles. I then tested whether mouse M1 has any neural activity associated with vocalization behavior. I combined electrophysiological recordings in LMC and OMC with video and audio monitoring of freely behaving and vocalizing males. I identified sparse populations of neurons with activity modulated over the production of bouts of USVs. This is the first report of vocalization-related activity in mouse M1. Finally, I developed a novel method to identify individual USV sources in pairs of vocalizing mice. This method used wearable miniature microphones to detect and assign USVs to a single animal based on simple amplitude differences. I reliably identified the individual responsible for the vocalization, and found that female mice produce far fewer USVs in a male- female pair than previously assumed. This method allows further study of the inter-individual vocal dynamics and behavior during the production of social USV. Overall, my findings support the continuum hypothesis of vocal learning. The direct cortical input from M1 to laryngeal motor neurons appears to be an evolutionary node to have faster control of vocal musculature. These same M1 regions have limited but present populations with vocalization-associated activity. This suggests that a sparse cortical representation for vocal muscles may be conserved. These results provide greater insight into the cortical control of vocalization in the mammalian brain and the evolution of more advanced vocal learning.
papers.abstract_zh: 语音通信用于向其他人传输一系列信息。虽然许多发声是与生俱来的,但有些物种可以学习改变它们的声音输出。这被称为声音学习,它是一种罕见的特征,也是人类口语和鸣禽歌曲的必要组成部分。对人类和鸣禽的比较研究表明,趋同的遗传和神经专业化可能会驱动这些习得的发声行为。这些高级发声学习者的两个关键特征是:i)前脑中专门的初级运动区域,其活动与发声相关;ii)从初级运动皮层到脑干发声运动神经元的密集单突触投射。我们实验室的工作表明,小鼠超声波发声 (USV) 系统具有一些与高级发声学习者相似的功能。USV 的产生是与生俱来的,但小鼠的音节库表现出上下文相关的变化。小鼠还可能拥有初级的喉部运动皮层(LMC),对疑核(Amb)中的喉部运动神经元有稀疏的直接投射,并且稀疏的群体对声带肌肉组织具有短潜伏期的功能控制。在这些研究之前,人们一直认为小鼠在超声波发声的产生中缺乏任何皮质参与。小鼠鸣叫的有限行为灵活性和声带肌肉前脑表征的证据表明,声乐学习可能存在于一个连续体中,小鼠处于连续体的有限末端,能够对 USV 的产生施加一些皮质控制。这一假设认为,声音学习不是一种全有或全无的能力,而是存在于一系列连续的声音行为中,并得到相应范围的神经和遗传专业化的支持。在这篇论文中,我建议通过研究初级运动皮层在小鼠发声行为中是否发挥作用来检验连续统假设。我首先描述了稀疏直接投射在声带肌肉控制中的作用。我使用复制缺陷 狂犬病 追踪来确认从 LMC 的第 5 层神经元到脑干喉部运动神经元存在稀疏投影,并且还发现前 M1 区域口面运动皮层 (OMC) 也具有直接的皮质运动神经元投影。然后,我使用 PLXNA1fl/fl;RBP4-CRE 转基因小鼠(从皮质到 Amb 的神经支配更密集)来测试该回路增强的功能后果。我使用配对的皮质内微刺激(ICMS)和肌电图(EMG),发现这些小鼠的喉部对皮质刺激的反应更快。这些发现表明,直接皮质运动神经元投射的增强可以产生更快的皮质对发声肌的控制。然后我测试了小鼠 M1 是否具有与发声行为相关的神经活动。我将 LMC 和 OMC 中的电生理记录与自由行为和发声的男性的视频和音频监控结合起来。我发现了稀疏的神经元群,其活动随着 USV 的产生而受到调节。这是小鼠 M1 发声相关活动的第一份报告。最后,我开发了一种新方法来识别发声小鼠中的单个 USV 源。该方法使用可穿戴微型麦克风来检测 USV,并根据简单的幅度差异将其分配给单个动物。我可靠地确定了负责发声的个体,并发现雌性小鼠在雄性小鼠和雌性小鼠中产生的 USV 比之前假设的要少得多。该方法可以进一步研究社交 USV 生产过程中个体间的声音动态和行为。总的来说,我的发现支持声音学习的连续统一体假设。从 M1 到喉部运动神经元的直接皮质输入似乎是一个进化节点,可以更快地控制发声肌肉组织。这些相同的 M1 区域具有有限但存在与发声相关活动的种群。这表明声带肌肉的稀疏皮质表征可能得以保留。这些结果让我们更深入地了解哺乳动物大脑中发声的皮层控制以及更高级的发声学习的 进化。

papers.title: Vaccines in Pregnancy: A Review of Guidelines
papers.abstract: Abstract Importance: Vaccination during pregnancy protects both the pregnant individual and the fetus from severe infectious diseases. Maternal immunization has expanded over the past decade, with new vaccines, robust safety data, and clear evidence of neonatal benefit through transplacental IgG transfer. Objective: To summarize current evidence regarding the safety, efficacy, and clinical recommendations for vaccines administered before and during pregnancy, outline strategies to address vaccine hesitancy, and provide an updated reference of vaccines recommended and contraindicated during pregnancy. Evidence Acquisition: Evidence synthesized from guidelines issued by the CDC, ACOG, SMFM, and major peer-reviewed publications including randomized trials, observational studies, vaccine safety surveillance systems, and meta-analyses. Literature informing disease burden, immune physiology, and perinatal outcomes associated with vaccine-preventable diseases also reviewed. Results: Influenza, Tdap, and COVID-19 vaccines demonstrate strong maternal and neonatal protective effects with excellent safety profiles. The RSV vaccine offers additional infant protection against severe lower respiratory tract disease. Several other vaccines (e.g., hepatitis A and B, meningococcal, polio, rabies) can be administered in pregnancy when clinically indicated. Live-attenuated vaccines remain contraindicated. Maternal immunization is most effective when integrated into routine prenatal care with onsite availability. Vaccine hesitancy can be mitigated through evidence-based counseling, addressing safety concerns, and improving the provider-patient trust relationship. Conclusion: Maternal immunization is safe, effective, and essential for preventing morbidity and mortality among pregnant individuals and infants. Relevance: This review provides clinicians with an updated guide for counseling, administering, and optimizing vaccine use before, during, and after pregnancy.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Importance: Vaccination during pregnancy protects both the pregnant individual and the fetus from severe infectious diseases. Maternal immunization has expanded over the past decade, with new vaccines, robust safety data, and clear evidence of neonatal benefit through transplacental IgG transfer. Objective: To summarize current evidence regarding the safety, efficacy, and clinical recommendations for vaccines administered before and during pregnancy, outline strategies to address vaccine hesitancy, and provide an updated reference of vaccines recommended and contraindicated during pregnancy. Evidence Acquisition: Evidence synthesized from guidelines issued by the CDC, ACOG, SMFM, and major peer-reviewed publications including randomized trials, observational studies, vaccine safety surveillance systems, and meta-analyses. Literature informing disease burden, immune physiology, and perinatal outcomes associated with vaccine-preventable diseases also reviewed. Results: Influenza, Tdap, and COVID-19 vaccines demonstrate strong maternal and neonatal protective effects with excellent safety profiles. The RSV vaccine offers additional infant protection against severe lower respiratory tract disease. Several other vaccines (e.g., hepatitis A and B, meningococcal, polio, rabies) can be administered in pregnancy when clinically indicated. Live-attenuated vaccines remain contraindicated. Maternal immunization is most effective when integrated into routine prenatal care with onsite availability. Vaccine hesitancy can be mitigated through evidence-based counseling, addressing safety concerns, and improving the provider-patient trust relationship. Conclusion: Maternal immunization is safe, effective, and essential for preventing morbidity and mortality among pregnant individuals and infants. Relevance: This review provides clinicians with an updated guide for counseling, administering, and optimizing vaccine use before, during, and after pregnancy.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要重要性:疫苗接种 在怀孕期间可以保护孕妇和胎儿免受严重传染病的侵害。过去十年来,随着新的 疫苗、可靠的安全数据以及通过胎盘 IgG 转移对新生儿有益的明确证据,孕产妇免疫接种范围不断扩大。目的:总结有关妊娠前和妊娠期间服用 疫苗 的安全性、有效性和临床建议的当前证据,概述解决 疫苗 犹豫的策略,并提供妊娠期间推荐和禁忌的 疫苗 的最新参考。证据获取:证据综合自 CDC、ACOG、SMFM 发布的指南和主要同行评审出版物,包括随机试验、观察性研究、疫苗 安全性 监测 系统和荟萃分析。还回顾了与 疫苗 可预防疾病相关的疾病负担、免疫生理学和围产期结局的文献。结果:流感、Tdap 和 COVID-19 疫苗 显示出强大的孕产妇和新生儿保护作用,且安全性优异。RSV 疫苗 为婴儿提供额外的保护,预防严重的下呼吸道疾病。当有临床指征时,其他几种 疫苗(例如甲型和乙型肝炎、脑膜炎球菌、脊髓灰质炎、狂犬病)可以在妊娠期间施用。减毒活 疫苗 仍然是禁忌的。将孕产妇免疫接种纳入常规产前护理并提供现场服务时最为有效。疫苗 的犹豫可以通过循证咨询、解决安全问题和改善提供者与患者的信任关系来缓解。结论:母亲免疫是安全、有效的,对于预防孕妇和婴儿的发病和 死亡率 至关重要。相关性:本综述为临床医生在怀孕前、怀孕期间和怀孕后提供咨询、管理和优化 疫苗 使用的最新指南。

Daily roundup Spark: Our top stories Over 90% of Human Rabies Cases in The US Aren't Detected, Study Finds Health01 September 2026 By Peter Dockrill Add ScienceAlert on Google Colorized transmission electron micrograph of rabies virus particles. (NIAID/Wikimedia Commons/CC BY 2.0) In February of last year, authorities confirmed the details of a grave medical accident. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) diagnosed a fatal rabies infection in a patient from Michigan. The circumstances of transmission were unusual. The deceased man, an organ recipient, had received a donated kidney infected with rabies. The source of the kidney was a man in Idaho who had died only weeks earlier, donating his organs for others in need. At the time of his death, nobody realized his body was infected with the deadly virus. Subsequent investigations revealed the Idaho man had recently been scratched by a skunk on his rural property – an infectious encounter that ultimately claimed his own life, and that of the man to whom he gave his kidney. Records show it was only the fourth time in US history that an organ transplant procedure had transmitted the rabies virus (Lyssavirus rabies) from an initially undiagnosed donor. But what if these kinds of records are wrong? Colorized transmission electron micrograph of rabies virus particles. (NIAID/Wikimedia Commons/CC BY 2.0) A new analysis published in Communications Health suggests that official figures may dramatically underestimate how many human cases of rabies are actually circulating in the US each year. According to researchers from the Pandemic Sciences Institute at the University of Oxford, the extremely low count of confirmed human rabies cases in the US each year – just 2.4 cases annually on average from 2000 to 2024 – seems much lower than it should be. The reason why it seems low is that a relatively high number of rabies cases are subsequently confirmed after infected organ transplants, like the sad case of the kidney recipient from Michigan. frameborder="0′′ allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen> Even though the Michigan patient fatality represents only the fourth known case of a transplanted fatal rabies infection – the first such instance occurring in 1978 – given how rare organ donation itself is, something just doesn't add up. "The instances of rabies transmission from initially undiagnosed deceased donors suggest that many human deaths due to rabies are not diagnosed as such, considering that only a small percentage of people dying in the US become organ and tissue donors," the researchers explain in a comment article. Per the researchers' calculations – which assume that the infected donors we know about faced an average nationwide level of risk of being infected with rabies – there should have been about 856 human cases of rabies in the years 2000–2024, whereas official records only document 60 confirmed cases during the period. In other words, from a purely statistical point of view, confirmed cases of human rabies that are recorded by the CDC may have missed over 90 percent of cases since the turn of the millennium, amounting to about 30 cases being missed each year on average. "Our central estimate suggests that only around 7 percent of human rabies cases in the general population were confirmed in recent years, and even its confidence limits indicate that, in the best-case scenario, only around 22 percent were diagnosed," the researchers write. "In order to argue that the reported number of rabies cases is consistent with complete surveillance, deceased donors would need to have a rabies risk approximately 14 times that of decedents in the general population." It's worth emphasizing that the researchers' calculations are only estimates based on statistical data, and they acknowledge they didn't take into account geographical, occupational, or socioeconomic factors in their analysis of rabies risk, which could help refine their projections. While it might seem unlikely that dozens of cases of rabies are being missed by doctors each year, that's exactly the scenario that plays out in the case of the infected organ donors, with the causes of their deaths only being discovered tragically late in each instance. In the case of the Idaho man, before his death he had difficulty swallowing and walking, experienced hallucinations, and was later found unresponsive at home after a presumed cardiac arrest. Related: US Man Dies From Rabies After Receiving Infected Kidney In another rabies-infected case reported in 2005, the donor experienced nausea, vomiting, brain hemorrhaging, and seizures before death. Later, when his rabies infection was discovered, his friends recalled he had mentioned being bitten by a bat. In both cases, though, nobody at the time recognized the fatal infection for what it was, presumably because the symptoms could have been explained by many other possible (and likely more probable) causes. For similar reasons, routine lab tests for organ transplants don't screen for rabies, both because it's a niche case and also because of the time pressure during transplant situations. "If rabies is not clinically suspected, laboratory testing for rabies is not routinely performed," the CDC explained in 2013, "as it is difficult for doctors to confirm results in the short window of time they have to keep the organs viable for the recipient." The findings are reported in Communications Health. This article was fact-checked by Rebecca Dyer and edited by Rebecca Dyer. While we pride ourselves on our process, we are only human. Daily roundup Spark: Our top stories Over 90% of Human Rabies Cases in The US Aren't Detected, Study Finds Health01 September 2026 By Peter Dockrill Add ScienceAlert on Google Colorized transmission electron micrograph of rabies virus particles. (NIAID/Wikimedia Commons/CC BY 2.0) In February of last year, authorities confirmed the details of a grave medical accident. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) diagnosed a fatal rabies infection in a patient from Michigan. The circumstances of transmission were unusual. The deceased man, an organ recipient, had received a donated kidney infected with rabies. The source of the kidney was a man in Idaho who had died only weeks earlier, donating his organs for others in need. At the time of his death, nobody realized his body was infected with the deadly virus. Subsequent investigations revealed the Idaho man had recently been scratched by a skunk on his rural property – an infectious encounter that ultimately claimed his own life, and that of the man to whom he gave his kidney. Records show it was only the fourth time in US history that an organ transplant procedure had transmitted the rabies virus (Lyssavirus rabies) from an initially undiagnosed donor. But what if these kinds of records are wrong? Colorized transmission electron micrograph of rabies virus particles. (NIAID/Wikimedia Commons/CC BY 2.0) A new analysis published in Communications Health suggests that official figures may dramatically underestimate how many human cases of rabies are actually circulating in the US each year. According to researchers from the Pandemic Sciences Institute at the University of Oxford, the extremely low count of confirmed human rabies cases in the US each year – just 2.4 cases annually on average from 2000 to 2024 – seems much lower than it should be. The reason why it seems low is that a relatively high number of rabies cases are subsequently confirmed after infected organ transplants, like the sad case of the kidney recipient from Michigan. frameborder="0′′ allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen> Even though the Michigan patient fatality represents only the fourth known case of a transplanted fatal rabies infection – the first such instance occurring in 1978 – given how rare organ donation itself is, something just doesn't add up. "The instances of rabies transmission from initially undiagnosed deceased donors suggest that many human deaths due to rabies are not diagnosed as such, considering that only a small percentage of people dying in the US become organ and tissue donors," the researchers explain in a comment article. Per the researchers' calculations – which assume that the infected donors we know about faced an average nationwide level of risk of being infected with rabies – there should have been about 856 human cases of rabies in the years 2000–2024, whereas official records only document 60 confirmed cases during the period. In other words, from a purely statistical point of view, confirmed cases of human rabies that are recorded by the CDC may have missed over 90 percent of cases since the turn of the millennium, amounting to about 30 cases being missed each year on average. "Our central estimate suggests that only around 7 percent of human rabies cases in the general population were confirmed in recent years, and even its confidence limits indicate that, in the best-case scenario, only around 22 percent were diagnosed," the researchers write. "In order to argue that the reported number of rabies cases is consistent with complete surveillance, deceased donors would need to have a rabies risk approximately 14 times that of decedents in the general population." It's worth emphasizing that the researchers' calculations are only estimates based on statistical data, and they acknowledge they didn't take into account geographical, occupational, or socioeconomic factors in their analysis of rabies risk, which could help refine their projections. While it might seem unlikely that dozens of cases of rabies are being missed by doctors each year, that's exactly the scenario that plays out in the case of the infected organ donors, with the causes of their deaths only being discovered tragically late in each instance. In the case of the Idaho man, before his death he had difficulty swallowing and walking, experienced hallucinations, and was later found unresponsive at home after a presumed cardiac arrest. Related: US Man Dies From Rabies After Receiving Infected Kidney In another rabies-infected case reported in 2005, the donor experienced nausea, vomiting, brain hemorrhaging, and seizures before death. Later, when his rabies infection was discovered, his friends recalled he had mentioned being bitten by a bat. In both cases, though, nobody at the time recognized the fatal infection for what it was, presumably because the symptoms could have been explained by many other possible (and likely more probable) causes. For similar reasons, routine lab tests for organ transplants don't screen for rabies, both because it's a niche case and also because of the time pressure during transplant situations. "If rabies is not clinically suspected, laboratory testing for rabies is not routinely performed," the CDC explained in 2013, "as it is difficult for doctors to confirm results in the short window of time they have to keep the organs viable for the recipient." The findings are reported in Communications Health. This article was fact-checked by Rebecca Dyer and edited by Rebecca Dyer. While we pride ourselves on our process, we are only human. news.content: Product of Caxton Local Media Saturday, September 5 2026 Caxton Network News Menu Search for Home Network News Lifestyle Lifestyle News Get It Homes Motoring Motoring News Sport Business About Us Complaints Elections 2026 The Citizen Search for HomeLNN News ContentDepartment of Agriculture records 15 human rabies deaths Department of Agriculture records 15 human rabies deaths Authorities urge pet owners to vaccinate animals as World Rabies Day approaches. 15 hours ago SAnews.gov.za 2 minutes read Facebook X LinkedIn Tumblr Pinterest WhatsApp Telegram Share via Email Print An image of a puppy receiving a rabies vaccine for illustration purposes only. Photo: 123RF/Caxton Local Media South Africa has recorded 15 human rabies deaths since the start of the year, according to the Department of Agriculture. An article by George Herald notes that the reported human fatalities include seven confirmed and two probable cases in the Eastern Cape, five confirmed cases in KZN and one confirmed case in Limpopo. Between January 1 and July 31, officials recorded 115 laboratory-positive animal rabies cases. Hotspot provinces The disease remains a serious threat across all nine provinces, with significant hotspots in Limpopo, KZN and the Eastern Cape. Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said preventing rabies requires action from pet owners, communities, healthcare workers and authorities. “Vaccinating dogs and cats, practising responsible pet ownership, reporting suspected cases and seeking prompt medical care after potential exposure are essential to preventing deaths,” Aucamp said. Preventable illness Although rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms develop, deaths are preventable through appropriate vaccination and timely post-exposure treatment. The infection can affect any mammal, including domestic animals, livestock, wildlife and humans. Regular vaccination of dogs and cats remains one of the most effective ways to prevent the spread of rabies and protect households and communities. Responsible pet ownership includes preventing the movement of unvaccinated animals, monitoring animals for unusual behaviour and reporting suspected cases to authorities. Emergency response Anyone bitten or scratched by a suspected rabid animal, or exposed to its saliva through a wound or mucous membrane, must immediately wash the affected area with soap and running water for at least 10 minutes. Medical attention should be sought without delay, as post-exposure treatment can prevent rabies when administered promptly and correctly. Community action The department is working through the National Rabies Advisory Group with stakeholders to raise awareness and strengthen measures to protect animal and human health. Veterinary and para-veterinary professionals, healthcare workers, government departments, policymakers, communities, pet owners and animal welfare organisations all play a role in prevention. Members of the public can contact local state or private veterinarians, animal health technicians or animal welfare organisations for advice on prevention and vaccination. Details of provincial veterinary services are available through the Department of Agriculture. World Rabies Day South Africa will join countries worldwide to mark World Rabies Day on September 28. This year’s theme, ‘Stronger Together’, highlights the need for co-operation between communities, animal and human health sectors, governments and international partners to eliminate rabies. Aucamp urged South Africans to take practical steps to protect themselves, their families, pets and communities. “Through responsible pet ownership and acting quickly, we are ‘Stronger Together’ in the fight against rabies,” Aucamp said. news.content_original: Product of Caxton Local Media Saturday, September 5 2026 Caxton Network News Menu Search for Home Network News Lifestyle Lifestyle News Get It Homes Motoring Motoring News Sport Business About Us Complaints Elections 2026 The Citizen Search for HomeLNN News ContentDepartment of Agriculture records 15 human rabies deaths Department of Agriculture records 15 human rabies deaths Authorities urge pet owners to vaccinate animals as World Rabies Day approaches. 15 hours ago SAnews.gov.za 2 minutes read Facebook X LinkedIn Tumblr Pinterest WhatsApp Telegram Share via Email Print An image of a puppy receiving a rabies vaccine for illustration purposes only. Photo: 123RF/Caxton Local Media South Africa has recorded 15 human rabies deaths since the start of the year, according to the Department of Agriculture. An article by George Herald notes that the reported human fatalities include seven confirmed and two probable cases in the Eastern Cape, five confirmed cases in KZN and one confirmed case in Limpopo. Between January 1 and July 31, officials recorded 115 laboratory-positive animal rabies cases. Hotspot provinces The disease remains a serious threat across all nine provinces, with significant hotspots in Limpopo, KZN and the Eastern Cape. Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said preventing rabies requires action from pet owners, communities, healthcare workers and authorities. “Vaccinating dogs and cats, practising responsible pet ownership, reporting suspected cases and seeking prompt medical care after potential exposure are essential to preventing deaths,” Aucamp said. Preventable illness Although rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms develop, deaths are preventable through appropriate vaccination and timely post-exposure treatment. The infection can affect any mammal, including domestic animals, livestock, wildlife and humans. Regular vaccination of dogs and cats remains one of the most effective ways to prevent the spread of rabies and protect households and communities. Responsible pet ownership includes preventing the movement of unvaccinated animals, monitoring animals for unusual behaviour and reporting suspected cases to authorities. Emergency response Anyone bitten or scratched by a suspected rabid animal, or exposed to its saliva through a wound or mucous membrane, must immediately wash the affected area with soap and running water for at least 10 minutes. Medical attention should be sought without delay, as post-exposure treatment can prevent rabies when administered promptly and correctly. Community action The department is working through the National Rabies Advisory Group with stakeholders to raise awareness and strengthen measures to protect animal and human health. Veterinary and para-veterinary professionals, healthcare workers, government departments, policymakers, communities, pet owners and animal welfare organisations all play a role in prevention. Members of the public can contact local state or private veterinarians, animal health technicians or animal welfare organisations for advice on prevention and vaccination. Details of provincial veterinary services are available through the Department of Agriculture. World Rabies Day South Africa will join countries worldwide to mark World Rabies Day on September 28. This year’s theme, ‘Stronger Together’, highlights the need for co-operation between communities, animal and human health sectors, governments and international partners to eliminate rabies. Aucamp urged South Africans to take practical steps to protect themselves, their families, pets and communities. “Through responsible pet ownership and acting quickly, we are ‘Stronger Together’ in the fight against rabies,” Aucamp said. This confirmation is based on comprehensive efforts to control rabies through vaccination programs and surveillance. The validation was announced on September 4, 2026, and highlights Bhutan's success in preventing rabies transmission from dogs to humans. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers were reported in the evidence provided. The WHO's validation indicates that the country has achieved a state where dog-transmitted rabies is no longer present, which is a critical milestone in global rabies elimination efforts. This achievement underscores the effectiveness of targeted interventions and collaboration with international health organizations.

news.content: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS TIMES au NEWSLETTER SIGNUP My account Log Out Sep 06, 6:54 AM AEST Business News Sports Technology Entertainment NEWSLETTER My account Log Out Australia edition Business News Sports Technology Entertainment Editions Australia India International Singapore United Kingdom United States NEWSLETTER Follow Us Editions Australia India International Singapore United Kingdom United States Life Health & Wellbeing (VIDEO) North Carolina Boy Faces Six Rabies Shots After Mobile Petting Zoo Goats Test Positive for the Virus A child's encounter with rabid goats at a petting zoo prompts urgent health measures in North Carolina. By Anthony Will Published 09/02/26 AT 12:46 AM AEST Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket North Carolina Boy Faces Six Rabies Shots After Mobile Petting Zoo Goats Test Positive for the Virus MOCKSVILLE, N.C. — A North Carolina family is racing through a series of rabies vaccinations for their 4-year-old son after learning that baby goats he petted at a mobile petting zoo tested positive for the virus, part of a broader public health response now underway across the state. Rebecca Lanning, 30, of Marion, said she received a call from her son's aunt last Friday informing her that her son had been exposed to rabies. The family had visited a dinosaur-themed exhibit in Mocksville 13 days earlier, on Aug. 15, an event that also featured food trucks, carnival games and a petting zoo where the boy fed baby goats by hand. "I didn't think anything of it until Friday, when his aunt called me and was like, 'Hey, we have a situation,'" Lanning said. The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services announced Friday that three baby goats from the petting zoo had tested positive for rabies. Those animals, along with a fourth goat suspected of carrying the virus, have since been euthanized. Lanning immediately took her son to the doctor, where he received the first two of six required doses of the rabies vaccine, a regimen known as post-exposure prophylaxis. The shots are administered after a possible exposure in an effort to stop the virus before it can take hold in the body. Once symptoms of a rabies infection begin, the disease, which attacks the brain and spinal cord, is almost always fatal. The vaccine is nearly 100% effective at preventing the disease, but only when it is administered before symptoms appear. People can become infected with rabies through contact with the saliva of an infected animal, or through a bite or scratch. Lanning said the uncertainty of her son's specific interactions with the goats has weighed on her heavily in the days since learning of the exposure. "My fear is that if he was feeding the goats, and he's 4, who's to say that he didn't touch his mouth or eyes?" Lanning said. "I don't want to bury my child." Rabies symptoms typically take weeks to months to appear after exposure, and can initially resemble the flu, including weakness, fatigue, fever and headaches. According to the North Carolina health department, people may also experience a prickling or itching sensation at the site where they were touched or bitten by an infected animal. As of Monday, the state health department said it did not have an estimate of how many people may have been exposed to the infected goats. The animals were part of a North Carolina-based mobile petting zoo operation called Farm Adventures, which had appeared at events across the state between July 28 and Aug. 23. Beyond the Mocksville dinosaur exhibit, the goats were also brought to private gatherings, including birthday parties and a back-to-school celebration, as well as a visit to an assisted living center. A representative for Farm Adventures did not respond to a request for comment. The company addressed the situation in a post on its Facebook page, stating that its goats, which were too young to have been vaccinated against rabies themselves, appeared to have contracted the virus after a skunk got into their enclosure. Skunks are among the animals most commonly known to carry and transmit rabies, along with bats, raccoons and foxes. In a statement, the North Carolina health department said it is "working with local health departments and healthcare systems to make sure rabies post-exposure prophylaxis is available to anyone who needs it," as officials work to identify and reach others who may have come into contact with the infected animals during their weeks on the road. The incident comes amid what public health officials say is a broader increase in rabies exposures nationally in recent years. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, roughly 1.4 million Americans are evaluated annually for possible rabies exposure, with about 100,000 people ultimately receiving post-exposure prophylaxis shots each year. Health officials continue to urge caution around wild and unfamiliar animals, along with prompt medical attention following any bite, scratch or direct contact with an animal's saliva, given how critical early treatment is to preventing the disease from becoming fatal. news.content_zh: 一名4岁的北卡罗来纳州男孩在接触宠物动物园的山羊后感染了狂犬病病毒,因此接受了六剂狂犬病治疗。这些山羊属于一家名为Farm Adventures的公司,其中三只被确认感染,另一只被怀疑感染。在发现感染后,这些动物被安乐死。男孩的姨妈于2026年8月25日告知其母亲Rebecca Lanning有关接触的情况,促使立即采取医疗措施。北卡罗来纳州卫生与人类服务部正与当地当局合作,确保任何可能接触过该病毒的人都能获得狂犬病(暴露后预防)药物。该公司表示,这些山羊很可能从浣熊身上感染了狂犬病病毒,而卫生部门尚未估计可能受影响的人数。一旦出现症状,狂犬病病毒几乎总是致命的,但如果在症状出现前使用疫苗,其有效性接近100%。此次事件突显了在接触野生动物或不熟悉的动物后及时寻求医疗帮助的重要性。

analysis_zh.time: 事件发生在2026年8月15日,当时男孩在宠物动物园与山羊互动。家人于 2026 年 8 月 25 日获悉暴露情况,男孩于 2026 年 8 月 25 日接受了前两次 狂犬病 注射。北卡罗来纳州卫生与公众服务部于 2026 年 8 月 25 日宣布了 狂犬病 病例。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该活动在北卡罗来纳州莫克斯维尔举行,涉及一个名为“农场冒险”的移动宠物动物园。受影响的人群包括这名男孩以及其他可能在2026年7月28日至8月15日期间出现在活动中与受感染山羊有过接触的人。
analysis_zh.event: 北卡罗来纳州一名 4 岁男孩在移动宠物动物园抚摸小山羊后接触到了 狂犬病病毒。北卡罗来纳州卫生与公众服务部证实,三只山羊的 狂犬病 检测呈阳性,第四只山羊疑似感染。作为公共卫生应对措施的一部分,男孩收到了 暴露后预防 (PEP) 疫苗接种。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 这一事件促使北卡罗来纳州采取了更广泛的公共卫生应对措施,官员们正在努力识别并联系其他可能接触过病毒的人。卫生部门尚未估计可能暴露的人数。一旦出现症状,狂犬病 几乎总是致命的,但如果在症状出现之前施用,疫苗 几乎 100% 有效。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 北卡罗来纳州卫生与公众服务部正在与当地卫生部门和医疗保健系统合作,确保提供 狂犬病 PEP。Farm Adventures 公司在其 Facebook 页面上讨论了这一情况,称山羊可能是从臭鼬那里感染了 狂犬病。卫生部门尚未提供对暴露人数的估计,男孩与山羊的具体互动仍不确定。

This is the first confirmed human exposure incident involving a laboratory-verified positive animal this year. Rabies is common throughout New York State, with the vast majority of cases in raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, and woodchucks. Authorities say avoiding contact is your absolute best way of protecting yourself from this fatal disease. Health officials say all wild animal bites should be reported to the county health department at 845-292-5910. Rabies is 100 percent fatal if not promptly treated with rabies post exposure prophylaxis. Officials also said pets should be kept up to date on rabies vaccinations. A vaccination clinic has been scheduled for September 16 at the Narrowsburg Firehouse from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. Pre-registration is requested by calling 845-292-5910. Another clinic is being scheduled in the Town of Rockland. Signs of rabies in wild animals include aggressive, uncharacteristic behavior, such as attacking objects of people; losing fear of humans; difficulty walking or staggering; paralysis of the legs or jaw, loss of coordination; difficulty swallowing and a fear of water; and drooling or foaming at the mouth. news.content_title: Possible rabies exposure in 7 NC counties after baby goats test positive
news.content: Rabies was detected in three baby goats which were in contact with many North Carolina residents through a mobile petting zoo, the N.C. Department of Health and Human Services warned . According to a Friday, Aug. 28 release, the N.C. DHHS and N.C. Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services were first notified of a potential rabies exposure among four baby goats at Farm Adventures in Harmony on Aug. 27. The goats are believed to have been exposed to rabies by a skunk that entered a pen where they were kept in late July. The N.C. State Laboratory of Public Health confirmed rabies in three of the baby goats on Aug. 28. The fourth goat was not tested but is also assumed to have been infected.
